To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found that there is an existence of limit cycles and that there is a pH front for realistic parameter ranges for the zero-dimensional representation of an enzyme-catalysed unbuffered hydrolysation reaction in a one dimensional membrane.
there exists a sufficient condition on parameters for the existence of limit cycle and that a pH front is present for the stationary solution of the full system.
the zero-dimensional system can exhibit a stable limit cycle and that the full system of PDEs has stationary solutions that are characterized by a pH front.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the existence of a stationary pH front and a limit cycle in the enzyme-catalized hydrolysis reaction.
a mathematical model of an enzyme-catalysed reaction in a one- and zero-dimensional membrane.

the existence of a stable limit cycle for a system of ordinary differential equations that is the zero-dimensional limit of a system of partial differential equation that describes an enzyme-catalysed reaction in a membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a limit cycle can be expected for a wide range of realistic parameter ranges and a pH front can be expected for all realistic parameter ranges.
for realistic parameter values the system exhibits limit cycles as well as pH fronts, depending on the initial conditions.
for a certain parameter region the system is bistable, i.e., it possesses two different steady states, one with and one without a pH front.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a limit cycle is possible only if the pH gradient is sufficiently steep, i.e., if the front width is sufficiently small.
the zero-dimensional model is a good model for the full system of PDEs.
the existence of a stable pH front for the full reaction-diffusion system is a sufficient condition for the existence of an unstable limit cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of a stationary pH front is not dependent on the existence of a steady state for the full system.
the existence of a front is independent of the zero-dimensional approximation.
the pH front is a stable solution of the system.
